title: Union Environment Minister chairs 92nd Meeting of the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
body_text: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, chaired the 92 nd Meeting of the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL), today in  New Delhi. As part of the policy agenda, the Standing Committee considered the report on Wildlife Week 2026, celebrated under the theme ‘Connecting Habitats, Thriving Wildlife’. The Minister highlighted the initiatives taken during the Wildlife Week 2026, including the tiger reintroduction in Buxa, the release of Great Indian Bustards in Rajasthan and the expansion of Project Cheetah to a third site, reflecting the Government's focus on tangible, science-based conservation outcomes on the ground. Further, Shri Yadav congratulated the awardees selected during the Wildlife Week, and highlighted that the frontline staff and local communities are the backbone of India's wildlife conservation efforts. The Minister then felicitated them for exemplary wildlife conservation work: Frontline Staff – Protection and Anti-Poaching: Late Shri Banoth Naveen (Telangana), Shri Hukai H. Zhimo (Nagaland) and Thiru V. Kumaresan (Tamil Nadu). Frontline Staff – Wildlife Monitoring and Special Skills: Shri Umesh Bharat Kalsarpe (Maharashtra), Shri AshwinsinhKiritsinhJadeja (Gujarat) and the Bahraich Human-Wildlife Conflict Management Group (Uttar Pradesh). Community Conservation Award: Shree MahavirMachchhimarSahakariMandali Ltd., Mangrol (Gujarat), for whale shark conservation, and Ponnuruvi Eco-Tourism Management Committee, Sirumalai Hills (Tamil Nadu). Nameri Tiger Reserve, Assam was also accredited under Conservation Assured | Tiger Standards (CA|TS). The 92 nd meeting of SC-NBWL was themed on ‘marine conservation’. Underscoring the need for strengthening the conservation of wildlife, both terrestrial and marine, presentations were made by the Scientists of Wildlife Institute of India on the following - Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) of Coastal and Marine Protected Areas; Pan-India Assessment and Monitoring of Marine Turtles; Milestones of Recovery of Dugongs and their Habitats in India (2016–2026); and , Mitigating the Impacts of Linear Infrastructure on Wildlife. These presentations highlighted the status and achievements in conservation of wildlife, especially related to the management effectiveness of marine protected areas, marine turtle and dugongs. The presentation of mitigation of linear infrastructure on wildlife highlighted on addressing the challenges on consequential impact on wildlife and the need for empowering a wide range of stakeholders, including infrastructure planners, builders, environmental consultants, wildlife managers, regulators, policymakers, and analysts. In line with the theme of marine wildlife conservation, several publications were released during the meeting, that highlight the Ministry’s conservation initiatives relating to marine biodiversity conservation. These include: Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) of Coastal and Marine Protected Areas: Presents the findings of the 2024–26 assessment covering 108 coastal and marine Protected Areas, highlighting management performance, best practices and priority areas for strengthening conservation. Pan-India Assessment and Monitoring of Marine Turtles: Undertaken by the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) under the Ministry’s Development of Wildlife Habitats scheme, the assessment covers three nesting seasons (2022–25), approximately 1,300 km of coastline and 360 beach stretches, providing insights into the nesting status of four marine turtle species. Milestones of Recovery of Dugongs and their Habitats in India (2016–2026): Documents a decade of conservation efforts under the CAMPA-funded programme implemented by WII, including the first drone-based dugong population estimate in Tamil Nadu (270 ± 16), identification of seagrass habitats and notification of India’s first Dugong Conservation Reserve in Palk Bay. Status of Arabian Sea Humpback Whale in India: Presents the findings of WII’s 2022–25 assessment, identifying seven potential sighting hotspots and highlighting threats, particularly entanglement in fishing gear, to guide future conservation interventions. Marine Turtle Knowledge Products: Three publications— Technical Protocol of Marking Marine Turtles , Tracking Marine Turtles in Indian Waters and Marine Turtles of India —were released as outcomes of the Marine Turtle Action Plan (2021–2026), providing scientific guidance for monitoring, research and conservation of marine turtles. In addition to the above, the Minister also released a document pertaining to small cat conservation - Field Manual on Small Cats . It c overs nine species of small cats found in India and provides practical guidance on species identification, field surveys and monitoring. The manual has been developed under the Government of India–GEF Small Cats Conservation Project, implemented by MoEFCC in collaboration with the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, with support from UNDP and the Global Tiger Forum. The Standing Committee also considered 133 proposals across the country involving activities such as roads, defence infrastructure, drinking water supply and other essential development works requiring wildlife clearance under the provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. The proposals were appraised on the basis of their ecological impacts, importance for public welfare and national development, and the adequacy of mitigation measures to ensure conservation of wildlife and their habitats and also ensure the target of green growth. ***** VM
